title: Ballot-committee money given at an official’s request by organizations with business before the City
question: Since 2023 State law limits what a local elected official may ask of a party to a contract or permit decision, ballot campaigns included. Which organizations that gave to a ballot committee at an official’s request had such business?
finding: From January 2023 to 2026-10-14, 25 contributions from organizations, $1,165,000 in all, went to ballot-measure committees at the request of a supervisor or mayor. 1 followed, within twelve months, a Board decision on a contract, lease or grant naming the giver: Autodesk gave $75,000 to “Stronger Muni for All, Mayor Lurie's Ballot Measure Committee” at Daniel Lurie’s request on 2026-03-18, 232 days after File 250673 (lease or property). 6 came from organizations that City offices’ own waiver papers name, under the same name or one beginning the same way, as parties they engaged or solicited ($637,500): Anthropic ($500,000, Daniel Lurie, 2026-03-23); Salesforce.com, Inc. ($50,000, Matt Dorsey, 2024-10-30); JPMorgan Chase & Co. PAC (FEC ID: C00128512) ($50,000, Daniel Lurie, 2026-08-25); The Prado Group ($17,500, Daniel Lurie, 2026-05-26); The Prado Group, Inc. ($10,000, Bilal Mahmood, 2026-05-14); Shorenstein Company, LLC ($10,000, Bilal Mahmood, 2026-05-29).
how: Contributions are the Form 114.5 reports of contributions to ballot-measure committees made at a City elective officer’s request. The Ethics Commission’s notice on the State rule says an official may not solicit more than $250 from a party to a covered proceeding while it is pending and “for 12 months after the agency renders a final decision on the matter”, for any campaign, “including ballot measure campaigns”; covered proceedings include “contracts (other than competitively bid, labor, or personal employment contracts)”. Each organization is looked up among the counterparties of passed Board contract, lease, loan and grant-agreement files (exact name, or one name beginning with the other, which the row’s file title lets a reader check); “days” counts from the Board’s decision to the contribution, and only a decision in the 365 days before it is counted in the finding. The waiver column looks the giver up among the organizations named in the behested-payment waiver papers and waiver reports read by the “influence records” analysis. “City paid” is the payment ledger since fiscal 2019 under exactly the same name.
limits: A contribution made at an official’s request and reported on this form is disclosed, and most givers here have no decision on record. The notice describes the rule; whether a given lease or agreement is a covered proceeding, whether the Mayor’s signature on a Board resolution makes the Mayor’s office “the agency”, and whether a company’s political committee counts as the party are questions for the Ethics Commission and the State commission, not answered in any file on disk. Labor agreements are outside the rule, and union contributions are listed without a file. A waiver paper naming an organization says City staff engaged with it for a stated civic purpose; it does not say the organization had a pending decision. Individuals who gave are counted nowhere here and never named.
